summary: Implemented a terminal-signature boundary in a disposable copy: a helper locates the final non-whitespace line using LF, CRLF and bare CR; signature removal and digest lookup operate only on that line; verification reads the terminal digest. The patch applied cleanly to a fresh copy and produced byte-identical source. The repaired matrix rejected CR-tail, LF-tail and CRLF-tail executable variants while accepting valid LF, CRLF, trailing-newline and trailing-space signatures. A 20-check regression matrix over HTTP, code and DNS template shapes passed, including body tampering, embedded digest-looking comments and a stripped-bytes equality check. The real template parser on repaired source reported the CR-tail file as unverified while still parsing the appended code request; the pristine parser reported the same file as verified with the code request present. A cross-version check showed pristine-signed and repaired-signed ordinary templates verify under both implementations. The official host evaluator has not run.
next_hint: The local repair closes the reproduced CR-tail and multiple-signature boundary for ordinary templates. Remaining limits are the missing official verdict, imported code-file signatures, zero-width-byte tails and exact parity with the pinned official image.
